findings.title: P5-4 requires the workspace lock before the chunk that creates it

source_refs.value: P5-4 — Report builder: `§14 atomic tmp+rename under `reports/.lock`; ... Error handling: lock contention → `WorkspaceLockedError` (§14, full lock impl in P5-6/with the writer)`
P5-6 — Files: `src/report/trend.ts`; the `reports/.lock` workspace-lock helper (`src/report/lock.ts` — *new file; see plan-gap 2*)
Dependency summary: `P5-1 → P5-2 → P5-4 → P5-5 → P5-6`

findings.rationale: A builder executing chunks forward-only cannot make P5-4 both write `report.json` under `reports/.lock` and import/reuse the canonical lock helper, because `src/report/lock.ts` is not created until P5-6. With the plan's type-aware per-chunk lint, P5-4 either fails at its commit point or duplicates the lock primitive, creating divergent report/trend write semantics.
findings.acceptance_check: Move `src/report/lock.ts` and `src/report/lock.test.ts` into P5-4 or a new P5-3.5 before P5-4; reviewer proof is `grep -R "withWorkspaceLock" src/report/json.ts src/report/trend.ts` showing both consumers use the same helper plus `npx vitest run src/report/lock.test.ts src/report/json.test.ts`.
findings.operator_decision_required_reason: High-severity data-integrity sequencing issue affects the shared write primitive used by report and trend writers.

findings.title: No chunk owns replacing CLI scan stubs with static/live/run orchestration

source_refs.value: P1-4 — `In P1 the subcommands parse + validate config + print help; scan bodies are stubs that later phases fill.`
Dependency summary: `P4-1 → P4-2 → P4-3 → P4-4/P4-5/P4-6 → P4-7   (gate→preflight→ratelimit→scanners→fixture)`

findings.rationale: The plan creates scanner wrappers and report builders, but it never names a live orchestration module or an integration chunk that connects `scan-source`, `scan-live`, and `run` from the P1 stubs to `scanRepos`, preflight, auth, probes, ZAP/Nuclei, and `buildReport`. P5-6 claims to wire `audit run` while depending only on report chunks, and P4-7's detailed dependency line contradicts the summary about needing scanners before the fixture/abort test. A builder can complete the listed chunks while leaving user-facing scan commands as stubs or only partially wired.
findings.acceptance_check: Add an integration chunk after P4-6 and before P4-7/P5-6 that owns `src/live/orchestrator.ts` and `src/cli.ts`; proof is `src/cli.test.ts` asserting `scan-source` calls `scanRepos`, `scan-live --dry-run` calls preflight without scanners, non-dry-run `scan-live` calls the live orchestrator with an `AllowedTarget`, and `audit run` passes scanner outputs into `buildReport`, plus `grep -R "stub" src/cli.ts` returning no scan-body stubs.
findings.operator_decision_required_reason: Architectural integration gap spans CLI, static scanning, live scanning, benchmark fixture, and report generation.

findings.title: Stable rule/check inventory is referenced but never created, and wildcard IDs are left in contracts

source_refs.value: P6-1 — `rule-inventory ↔ corpus cross-check now covers all 11 rules + 3 wrapped families + each live `checkId` family`

findings.rationale: Benchmark coverage, SARIF help URIs, remediation packs, fingerprints, and docs all depend on exact stable IDs, but the plan never creates a canonical inventory file and leaves ZAP/Nuclei IDs as wildcards. That makes the corpus cross-check and `docs/rules/<ID>.md` completeness tests underspecified, and different builders could mint incompatible IDs in wrappers, docs, SARIF, and fix packs.
findings.acceptance_check: Add a canonical inventory such as `src/rules/inventory.ts` plus `src/rules/inventory.test.ts`; proof is that the test asserts every inventory ID has the required corpus/live-fixture expectation and `docs/rules/<id>.md`, and `grep -R "ZAP-P-\*\|ZAP-A-\*\|NUCLEI-\*" src docs benchmark rules` returns no wildcard contract IDs.
findings.operator_decision_required_reason: Stable identifiers are cross-cutting contracts for benchmark, reporting, SARIF, and remediation, so the exact inventory must be settled before builders mint IDs.

findings.title: Several chunks declare edits outside their file/dependency rows

source_refs.value: P1-1 — Depends on: none. `This chunk adds the `benchmark`/`schemas` npm scripts + a `bin` entry and pins the TS runner (`tsx`) per plan-gap 1`
P7-3 — Files: `src/report/html.ts`; test `src/report/html.test.ts`; wire `audit report --format html` (stub from P5-6 now real)

findings.rationale: The plan's convention says each chunk lists exact files, but P1-1 modifies `package.json`/lockfile and possibly dev dependencies without listing them, while P7-3 modifies the CLI and relies on the P5-6 report stub without listing `src/cli.ts` or depending on P5-6. Builders following only the file rows can miss required edits; builders following prose can touch files outside the reviewable chunk surface.
findings.acceptance_check: Update P1-1's file row to include `package.json` and the lockfile, and update P7-3's file/dependency rows to include `src/cli.ts`, `src/cli.test.ts`, and `P5-6`; reviewer proof is `grep -n "package.json"` in P1-1 and `grep -n "src/cli.ts"` in P7-3 of the final plan.

findings.title: Judgement-heavy UI and documentation chunks lack reviewer-auditable acceptance artefacts

source_refs.value: P7-2 — `acceptance is shape-match to the locked prototypes + plain-language vocabulary presence, verified by the pr-reviewer/mockup reference at review time, plus `npx eslint` on `ui/**`.`
P8-6 — `Test-first/G1 acceptance: doc completeness reviewed at PR; `npx eslint` n/a.`

findings.rationale: The plan explicitly avoids SPA component tests, which may be acceptable under its framing, but the replacement evidence is only reviewer judgement. P8-6 similarly says the doc is reviewed at PR with no concrete checklist or grepable contract. A context-free builder has no artefact to produce, and a reviewer has no stable evidence trail for prototype/vocabulary/doc completeness.
findings.acceptance_check: Add concrete acceptance artefacts: for P7-2 require `docs/ui-prototype-mapping.md` with one row per locked prototype screen and a grepable `ui/src/vocabulary.ts` normative-term export; for P8-6 require `docs/fix-workflow.md` headings or checklist entries matching `standard Claude Code action`, `audit-fix label`, `manual fallback`, `fingerprint marker`, and `token scopes`.
